input.quote: Garman agrees to indemnify Sparkling and hold it harmless from any and all losses, damages and expenses including without limitation, court costs, arbitration fees, penalties, fines, amounts paid in settlement of claims and reasonable legal fees and expenses of investigation (collectively the "Losses") which Sparkling or any of its respective officers or directors may incur due to a breach of this warranty.
input.rationale: Section 13 contains a Vendor-side IP indemnity: Garman warrants it owns/controls all rights necessary and has granted no conflicting liens or encumbrances, and indemnifies Sparkling (and its officers and directors) for all Losses, including settlement amounts and reasonable legal fees, arising from breach of that warranty; if the Work is held infringing and enjoined, Garman must procure the right to use, procure an equivalent element, or replace/modify at its own expense (p0091-p0093). There is no reciprocal or one-way Sparkling indemnity anywhere in the agreement, and Section 15's damages limitation expressly does not apply to breaches of Section 13, so the indemnity is not capped. This sits at (and in respects such as the absence of customer-modification/combination exclusions exceeds) the fallback position of a Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions and remedies, so we do not redline it. Noted short of preferred, but not material enough to flag: there is no express duty to "defend"/control the defence, no refund remedy, no extension to breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach or gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and the ten calendar day claim-notice period is tighter than our usual "prompt notice" standard.
